title: Maple Pecan and Bacon Cookies
story: Bacon in a cookie is the kind of idea that sounds like it came from a menu with too many words on it. The maple is in the dough, not a glaze, which means the flavor is in every bite. Cook the bacon until it's completely crispy before it goes in. Chewy bacon in a cookie is its own punishment.

items.text: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
½ cup crispy cooked bacon, crumbled (about 6 strips)

steps.text: Cook about 6 strips of bacon until completely crispy — oven method works well: 400°F on a rack for 15–18 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Bacon should be deeply browned and rigid, not chewy. Chewy bacon stays chewy in the cookie.

steps.text: Drain on paper towels and let cool completely before crumbling. Warm bacon will melt into the dough and disappear instead of giving you distinct pieces.
Whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, and ½ tsp fine salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat ½ cup room-temperature butter, ½ cup maple syrup, and ½ cup packed brown sugar together until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: The maple syrup makes this wetter than a standard creamed mixture — it won't get pale and fluffy. Look for a smooth, glossy consistency with no lumps of butter.

steps.text: Beat in 1 large egg and 1 tsp vanilla extract until fully combined.
Add the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Fold in 1 cup roughly chopped pecans and ½ cup crumbled bacon.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls — the maple syrup makes this dough stickier than most. Lightly oiled hands help. Place 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.

steps.donenessCue: Edges should be golden brown and the tops just set. The maple sugar caramelizes faster than granulated sugar — don't walk away in the last few minutes.

steps.text: Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt while still warm if using.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Replace 2 tbsp of the butter with reserved bacon fat — it deepens the smoky flavor in a way that's hard to place but impossible to ignore.
Toast the pecans in a dry skillet for 3 minutes before chopping. The difference is noticeable.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes before rolling — the maple syrup makes it sticky, and cold dough is much easier to handle.
Make a maple glaze: whisk ½ cup powdered sugar with 2 tbsp maple syrup until smooth and drizzle over cooled cookies.
Add a pinch of cayenne to the dry ingredients — it doesn't make the cookies spicy, but it makes the bacon taste more like bacon.
storage: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days — the bacon makes these more perishable than a standard cookie. Bring to room temperature before serving. Freeze for up to 2 months.
